question.text: A lift of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is descending with speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Its supporting cable begins to slip thus allowing it to fall with a constant acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The kinetic energy of the lift at the end of fall through to a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kJ</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Given, u=2 m s-1, a=2 m s-2, s=6 m

Using kinematics third equation of motion, final speed of lift is v2=u2+2as

⇒v=22+226

=4+24=28 m s-1

Now, kinetic energy of the lift is KE=12mv2

=12(500)28

=7000 J

=7 kJ
